name: The Augustan Frequency: Collected Verse 2188-2210
creator: Isolde Kamau-Petrov
description: A major career retrospective collecting twenty-two years of work by GLMZ's most celebrated living poet, whose verse moves fluidly between the intimate and the geopolitical, often within the same stanza. Kamau-Petrov, now in her late sixties and living in Tier 3, writes in a form she developed called 'neural prosody' — structured to create specific rhythmic effects in BCI-assisted reading that do not exist in text-only consumption, though the poems also function on the page. The physical edition, published by a Tier 4 independent press, is considered one of the most beautiful book objects produced in GLMZ in the last decade.
medium: physical hardcover (limited, premium); neural feed (BCI-optimized version); audio recitation by the author
cultural_impact: Widely considered the definitive literary document of what it feels like to be alive in GLMZ across multiple tiers and decades; the collection is taught in Tier 3-4 schools and has been translated into seven linguistic blends.
controversy: A small but vocal faction of literary critics argues that 'neural prosody' is a corponation-friendly innovation that privileges augmented readers and effectively creates a two-tier reading experience that mirrors social stratification — a charge Kamau-Petrov finds genuinely interesting rather than offensive.
story_hooks: A poem written in 2191 and included in the collection contains imagery that precisely describes a building that wasn't constructed until 2204 — and Kamau-Petrov, when asked, goes very quiet.

Someone has been producing forged physical copies of the collection with altered poems — the alterations are subtle, brilliant, and ideologically opposed to everything Kamau-Petrov has ever said she believes.
The author is dying and has asked a former student to destroy a specific set of unpublished work; the student is not sure they can.
